questions.prompt: Which statement is part of the cell theory?

options.text: All cells arise from pre-existing cells
All organisms are made of a single cell
Cells are visible to the naked eye
Viruses are the basic units of life

questions.explanation: Cell theory says living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and cells come from pre-existing cells. It does not say that every organism is unicellular, since many are multicellular.

questions.prompt: A key difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is that prokaryotes
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic DNA lies free in the cytoplasm, in a nucleoid. They do have genetic material and a cell membrane, and they are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is the main site of ATP production in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration. Chloroplasts also make ATP, but only in plant cells and as part of photosynthesis, so animal cells do not have them.

questions.prompt: Which organelle modifies, packages and sorts proteins for secretion?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus processes and dispatches proteins in vesicles. Rough ER makes and folds proteins first, so it is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Which process moves substances across a membrane against a concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Active transport uses ATP to pump substances against the gradient. Facilitated diffusion uses carrier proteins but moves substances down the gradient, with no energy.

questions.prompt: A red blood cell is placed in distilled water. It will
questions.explanation: Water enters the cell by osmosis because the inside is more concentrated than the surroundings. A cell shrinks only in a solution more concentrated than its contents.

questions.prompt: Extreme heat denatures an enzyme because it

options.text: adds extra amino acids to the enzyme
removes the enzyme's bonds to ATP
changes the three-dimensional shape of the active site

questions.explanation: Heat breaks the weak bonds that hold the tertiary structure, so the active site no longer fits the substrate. The enzyme is not used up, but it loses its shape.

questions.prompt: In photosynthesis, the light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) take place in the
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma. The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes, which is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: How many net ATP molecules are produced by glycolysis from one molecule of glucose?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis makes 4 ATP but uses 2, so the net gain is 2. The figures 36 and 38 are for the complete aerobic breakdown of glucose.

questions.prompt: In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments pyruvate to ethanol and CO2. Lactic acid is the product in human muscle cells during anaerobic respiration.

questions.prompt: During which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
questions.explanation: Anaphase is when the centromeres divide and chromatids are pulled apart. In metaphase they line up at the equator, which is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs during
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes pair and exchange segments in prophase I, which creates genetic variation. Mitosis has no pairing of homologues.

questions.prompt: A DNA sample contains 30% adenine. The percentage of cytosine in the sample is
questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine, so T is also 30%, leaving 40% for G + C, shared equally. Cytosine is 20%. The value 40% is the combined G + C. The value 70% is simply everything that is not adenine, and it includes thymine as well as the two other bases.

questions.prompt: Two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt) are crossed. The expected ratio of tall to short offspring is
questions.explanation: Tt x Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt, so three show the dominant trait and one shows the recessive. A 1 : 1 ratio comes from a test cross. A 1 : 3 ratio is the reverse of the true result, and 2 : 1 appears only when one homozygous genotype is lethal.

questions.prompt: In binomial nomenclature, the scientific name of a species consists of

options.text: the family name followed by the genus name
the genus name followed by the species name
the kingdom name followed by the class name
the species name followed by the phylum name

questions.explanation: A binomial such as Homo sapiens gives the genus (capital initial) then the species (lower case), both italicised. The family is a broader rank and does not form part of the two-part name.

questions.prompt: The cell wall of fungi is made mainly of
questions.explanation: Fungal walls contain chitin. Plant walls are made of cellulose, which is the nearest wrong choice, and bacterial walls contain peptidoglycan.

questions.prompt: A microscope has a 10x eyepiece and a 40x objective lens. The total magnification is
questions.explanation: Total magnification = eyepiece x objective = 10 x 40 = 400x. Adding the numbers gives 50, which confuses the method.

questions.prompt: Which plant tissue transports sucrose from the leaves to other parts of the plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem carries sugars (translocation). Xylem carries water and minerals upward, and it is the nearest wrong choice.

questions.prompt: Which change would INCREASE the rate of diffusion across a membrane?
questions.explanation: A bigger difference in concentration drives faster net movement. A thicker membrane and smaller area slow it, and a lower temperature reduces particle movement.

questions.prompt: Which feature is characteristic of viruses?

options.text: They have a cell membrane and ribosomes
They can reproduce only inside a host cell

questions.explanation: Viruses lack cellular machinery and use the host's. They have no membrane-bound organelles, and they are far smaller than bacteria.
